title: Venue-operator model for gaming machines; end of the Tatts-Tabcorp duopoly (Victoria)
summary: From 16 August 2012 Victorian pubs and clubs own or lease their gaming machines under 10-year entitlements, replacing the Tatts and Tabcorp gaming operator duopoly.
direction_rationale: Removing the upstream duopoly lets venues capture machine revenue and compete directly, but entitlement auctions and caps may concentrate venue ownership.
comparison: NSW and Queensland, where venues already owned their machines

verified.notes: Date from the regulator's 2011-12 annual report.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Pubs and clubs own or lease gaming machines under ten-year entitlements, replacing the Tatts and Tabcorp duopoly. Entitlement auctions and caps may concentrate venue ownership.

marks.reason: Removes the upstream duopoly, letting venues operate machines directly.

assessment.confidence_note: Gambling harm, which the caps address, is not weighed here.

responsible.note: The Minister for Casino, Gaming and Liquor Regulation administers the Gambling Regulation Act 2003.
